articles.title: MAKE BUSINESS MONEY MOVE FASTER
articles.summary:
Your business moves quickly. Your money should, too. Stripe Treasury brings payments and financial tools together, helping you pay vendors, send payouts, issue cards, and manage cash flow with less complexity. Instead of stitching together separate systems, your team can manage more financial workflows on the platform you already use for payments. That means less time navigating disconnected tools and more time focused on your business.

From everyday operations to your next stage of growth, Stripe Treasury gives you flexible infrastructure to move money faster, streamline how work gets done, and build financial operations that can adapt as you scale.

articles.title: EXPLORE STRIPE TREASURY
ALWAYS ON: WHAT IT'S LIKE BEING A TWENTY-SOMETHING FOUNDER IN THE AGE OF AI
articles.summary: Young AI startups often try to win over big enterprise buyers through sheer speed. First Round interviewed young leaders behind Gumloop and Reducto about running companies in this wave. A buyer asked Gumloop for new features at 10 AM and got a walkthrough of them live by 5 PM, which Gumloop says changed how the buyer saw the team even though the features went unused. Enterprise deals still brought growing pains, with Reducto mishandling early procurement and Gumloop eventually hiring experienced enterprise sellers. The leaders also separate their own hours from what they ask of staff.

articles.title: THE AGENTIC STORY ON THE EVE OF THE 2026 HOLIDAY SEASON
articles.summary: Agentic payments continue to grow fast. Airfare and retail are currently the dominant spend categories. More than half of consumers who make one agentic purchase come back to make at least a second, typically in the same spending category.

articles.title: CRAZY AGENT SCALE: COMPANIES ALL-IN ON AI
articles.summary: Experts demonstrated what pushing agents to their limits looks like today at the Crazy Agent Scale event at Sutter Hill Ventures. Clement Pang, co-founder of Wavefront, shared lessons from building an open-source system for large-scale agent orchestration. David Cramer, co-founder of Sentry, discussed using one agent for the whole company. Shawn Wang, an AI engineer, discussed tiny teams and internal tools. Quinn Slack, CEO of Amp and Co-founder of Sourcegraph, shared how to use agents to scale. John Hayes talked about running a software factory in production.

articles.title: A TRANSPARENT PRICING MODEL FOR AI
articles.summary: AI software companies keep redoing their pricing because model costs have plunged and customers are moving to cheaper open models. The automation startup Gumloop switched to passing token and compute costs through to customers plus an 8% orchestration fee, with a separate enterprise platform fee. Gumloop reports that its Pro trial conversion rate rose 42% after the switch, while open-weight models grew from nothing to a real share of usage. Existing contracts stay in place until renewal, and Gumloop gives up pricing control since token revenue now moves with outside model prices.

articles.title: HOW TO BUILD A KNOWLEDGE FACTORY
articles.summary: Making AI work for a company requires better knowledge, not just more context. Agents need knowledge of how the company works, what standards for operating it has in place, and where data is stored and how it's accessed. This knowledge is often tacit, implicit, and scattered. Companies need to collect, curate, and maintain a representation of that knowledge to pass to agents.

articles.title: EXPANSION ABM PLAYBOOK
articles.summary: Selling into other divisions of an existing customer is often easier than winning a cold account. A marketing firm ran an expansion pilot for TestRail that reportedly built $2.4 million in qualified sales pipeline over six months. The playbook starts with customer champions who help build private case studies under NDA and co-host educational events. Marketing owns the content while sales reps map each unit's buyers. Reps use webinar responses and content-hub activity to choose follow-up.

articles.summary: Causal launched in 2019 and was acquired in 2024. It did not achieve a huge outcome by VC standards, but it was still a financial success. The team started with an idea for a cool product and then tried to build a business around it. This post tells the story of the startup, the lessons it learned, and why the founders' original plan is not advisable for other startups.
